question: Does it just write generic filler?
answer: No — and the scope section is where you will notice. Pilot writes deliverables as countable items with an exclusions list, because that is what protects the margin. Anything it genuinely cannot infer from the brief it marks as an open question rather than quietly inventing a number.

question: Where do the prices come from?
answer: Two places: the rates you set once when you sign up, and anonymised ranges from comparable projects in your region. You always see the arithmetic, and you can override any line — everything downstream re-prices itself when you do.

question: Can I use my own template and terms?
answer: Yes. Upload a proposal you have already sent and Pilot will match its structure, headings, and tone on everything it writes afterwards. Paste in your own contract clauses and it will use those instead of the defaults.

question: Do my clients need an account?
answer: Never. A proposal goes out as a link that opens in any browser, or as a PDF attachment if that is how your client prefers to work. You still see when the link was opened.

question: What happens to my data?
answer: Your briefs, rates, and proposals are yours. We do not train shared models on your content, and you can export everything or delete your account outright from the settings page at any time.

question: Is it worth it if I only send two proposals a month?
answer: Probably, if either one is worth more than a few thousand. Most of the value is in pricing confidently and scoping tightly rather than in the time saved — but the time saved is roughly two hours per proposal, which tends to settle the argument.
